note: What the Basic Finner's single-wedge fins add to its zero-lift drag that HPR Sim's design can't draw, at DREV-TM-9703's six Mach numbers inside the envelope (M1.14b2; docs/research/basic-finner-wedge-drag.md). The faces' pressure with the shock attached is computed by hpr_aero::blunt_tip::wedge_pressure_coefficient and not typed. detached_faces is the faces' drag where the bow wave stands off (Mach 1.077): W. G. Vincenti and C. B. Wagoner, Transonic Flow Past a Wedge Profile with Detached Bow Wave, NACA Report 1095, 1952, Fig. 7 (p. 9, PDF p. 12), the front wedge's generalized drag coefficient (gamma+1)^(1/3) c_d/(t/c)^(5/3) read by pixel measurement at the similarity parameter (M^2 - 1)/((gamma+1) t/c)^(2/3); the report's front wedge, with t/c = 0.04 on its double wedge's chord, is the fin's wedge, and it states the front half's results hold for any wedge ending in a sharp convex corner (p. 3). trailing_edge_base is the trailing edges' base-drag coefficient on their own area, minus the base-pressure coefficient, of a two-dimensional blunt trailing edge with a turbulent boundary layer, the band spanned by two figures read by pixel measurement: S. F. Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, 1965, Fig. 11 of Chapter XVI (p. 16-11), measured, and E. S. Love, NACA TN 3819, 1957, Fig. 5 (p. 34), Chapman's and another compilation of measurements and Love's own estimates. At Mach 1.077 the two disagree (Hoerner's measurements 0.59 to 0.72, Love's estimates 0.43 to 0.49, his compiled data starting near Mach 1.16), so the band spans both. Read 2026-11-16.
